clue.text: Dangerous vessel about at sea

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so the letters of the word before are jumbled

explanation.surface: A warning about a hazardous ship somewhere out on the ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' looks like part of the nautical picture but is the anagram signal: ABOUT is rearranged into UBOAT.
explanation.definitionFit: A German submarine of the world wars was a deadly threat to Allied shipping.

clue.text: Comprehensive opened — see inside

indicators.note: inside places the word for see within the word for opened

parts.note: undid means unfastened or opened
vide is Latin for see, used in references

explanation.surface: A comprehensive school has been opened; go and look inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inside' is the container signal. Vide is Latin for 'see', familiar from footnotes; 'Comprehensive' reads as a school but is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Undivided attention is whole and complete, total in its scope.

clue.text: Jude was not easy to read

definitions.text: Jude was not easy to read

parts.words: Jude was not easy to read
parts.note: Hardy's novel title gives Jude an epithet meaning hard to make out, and the clue plays on that

explanation.surface: Someone named Jude was a hard person to read.
explanation.walkthrough: Thomas Hardy's novel is 'Jude the Obscure'; the word also means hard to understand.
explanation.definitionFit: The adjective means unclear or difficult to understand, and is Jude's epithet in Hardy's title.

clue.text: Deftness of stroke

definitions.meaning: skill or a sure hand, as in a light hand at the piano
a stroke as a gentle caress or a brief contact

explanation.definitionFit: The word means both skill of handling and a light contact, like a caress.

clue.text: One assisting criminal to get handbag, say

definitions.meaning: in law, a helper of a lawbreaker before or after the crime
a fashion extra such as a bag, belt or scarf

explanation.surface: Someone helping a crook makes off with a handbag.
explanation.definitionFit: The word means both an accomplice in crime and a fashion item worn to complement clothes.

clue.text: Not with profit, in a way

indicators.note: in places the word for profit inside the other pieces

parts.note: St is the abbreviation for street, a way
gain means profit

explanation.surface: Opposing financial gain, after a fashion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in' is the container signal. The OCR dropped the space in 'a way'; read as 'to some extent', the phrase hides A and a street.
explanation.definitionFit: Against is the opposite of with, in the sense of opposing.

clue.text: Plant in money-making situation opened by Conservative

indicators.note: opened by places the party letter at the start of what follows

parts.note: at means in, as in at home
the Mint is where coins are made

explanation.surface: A factory plant in a lucrative business is opened by a Tory politician.
explanation.walkthrough: 'money-making situation' literally means the place where money is made: the Mint.
explanation.definitionFit: Catmint is a herb that cats find intoxicating, also called catnip.

clue.text: Bet so ably — result of him being crooked?

definitions.text: Bet so ably — result of him being crooked?

indicators.note: crooked means bent or twisted, so the letters are twisted into a new order

explanation.surface: A punter's lucky streak comes from a dishonest racing insider.
explanation.walkthrough: 'crooked' works twice in the surface: dishonest, and as the anagram signal for BET SO ABLY.
explanation.definitionFit: A stable lad who tips off gamblers about horses would make their wagers shrewd.

clue.text: Herb's old ass turned up

indicators.note: in a down entry, turned up means the word is read from bottom to top

parts.note: an onager is a wild ass of Asia

explanation.surface: A herb belonging to an old donkey that has appeared.
explanation.walkthrough: 'turned up' is the reversal signal in this down entry. An onager is a wild ass, an old crossword favourite.
explanation.definitionFit: Oregano is an aromatic herb of Mediterranean cooking.

clue.text: They have their ups and downs, with strings attached

definitions.text: They have their ups and downs, with strings attached

parts.words: They have their ups and downs, with strings attached
parts.note: reads like people in a conditional relationship, but describes a spinning toy on a cord

explanation.surface: Some people have a turbulent relationship that comes with conditions.
explanation.definitionFit: These toys rise and fall on a string wound round their axle.

clue.text: Person fighting far away without back-up

indicators.note: without here has its old sense of outside, so one piece surrounds the other

parts.note: far away means distant

indicators.note: back tells us the word up is read in the opposite direction

explanation.surface: A combatant left alone, a long way off with no reinforcements.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is the container signal, in its old sense 'outside'. 'back-up' reads as reinforcements but splits into 'back', the reversal signal, and 'up'.
explanation.definitionFit: A disputant is someone engaged in an argument or quarrel, a combatant in words.

clue.text: Imitation fabrics doctor removed from front

indicators.note: says the abbreviation for doctor is taken off the start of the cloth word

parts.note: drapery is cloth or fabrics collectively

explanation.surface: Fake cloth, with a medic taken away from the front of the shop.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking DR from DRAPERY leaves APERY.
explanation.definitionFit: Apery is mimicry, copying others the way apes are said to.

clue.text: Composer, poet and playwright

parts.note: Henry Vaughan was a 17th-century Welsh metaphysical poet
Tennessee Williams was the American dramatist

explanation.surface: A list of three artistic professions.
explanation.walkthrough: The surface seems to list three people; in fact the poet's and playwright's surnames join to name the composer.
explanation.definitionFit: Ralph Vaughan Williams was an English composer of symphonies and the Lark Ascending.

clue.text: Apply pressure to mould the German players

parts.note: die is a German word for the
the cast is the set of actors in a show

explanation.surface: Instructions to lean on a troupe of German actors.
explanation.walkthrough: 'mould' looks like a verb about pressuring the actors, but it belongs to the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Die-casting forms metal objects by forcing molten metal into a mould under pressure.

clue.text: Element — one more found here that in America

definitions.text: Element — one more found here that in America

parts.words: Element — one more found here that in America
parts.note: British spelling of this metal has one more letter i than the American spelling

explanation.surface: A substance more plentiful in Britain than in the United States.
explanation.walkthrough: 'that' is a slip for 'than'. 'one more' sounds like more of the substance but means one more letter I.
explanation.definitionFit: The light metal with symbol Al is spelt with an extra i in British English.

clue.text: Novel a bit old for publication

indicators.note: novel means new or fresh, so the letters are made into a new arrangement

explanation.surface: A book a little dated for being printed.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Novel' reads as a book but signals an anagram of A BIT OLD.
explanation.definitionFit: A tabloid is a popular newspaper of small page size.

clue.text: Escaped rising water, possibly, in some Dutch vessels

indicators.note: in a down entry, rising means the word reads from the bottom up

parts.note: fled means escaped

indicators.note: possibly signals the letters of water could be another arrangement

explanation.surface: Water escaped upward and possibly leaked into some Dutch ships.
explanation.walkthrough: FLED reversed gives DELF; WATER rearranged gives TWARE. 'vessels' means pots, not ships.
explanation.definitionFit: Delftware is glazed pottery from Delft, in the Netherlands, so its pots and jugs are Dutch containers.

clue.text: Expert carrying gold left in fallback position

indicators.note: carrying means holding something within, so one piece goes inside another

parts.note: deft means skilful or expert
Au is the chemical symbol for gold

explanation.surface: A specialist holding gold has been left in a backup spot.
explanation.definitionFit: A default is the option that applies automatically when nothing else is chosen.

clue.text: Clown keeps one very cheerful

indicators.note: keeps means holds inside, so the clown's name contains the other pieces

parts.note: Feste is the jester in Shakespeare's Twelfth Night
one is I in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A clown keeps one person in very good spirits.
explanation.definitionFit: Festive means jolly, in a celebratory mood.

clue.text: Plans requiring sensitivity in careful sketches originally

parts.note: tact is sensitivity in dealing with people

indicators.note: originally points to the first letters of the following words

explanation.surface: Plans that need a delicate touch in careful drawings.
explanation.definitionFit: Tactics are schemes or methods for reaching a goal.

clue.text: Lament getting to last resort, that's very clear

parts.note: to cry is to wail or lament

indicators.note: resort read as re-sort, sorting the letters of the word last again

explanation.surface: A mourner reaches a final refuge, and things become plain.
explanation.walkthrough: 'last resort' looks like a set phrase, but 'resort' means re-sort, rearranging LAST into STAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Something described as crystal is perfectly transparent, as in crystal-clear water.

clue.text: Boy entering church on green

parts.note: CE is the Church of England
a lad is a boy

explanation.surface: A boy going into church on the village green.
explanation.walkthrough: 'green' looks like the village green but is the colour.
explanation.definitionFit: Celadon is a pale greyish-green colour, also a glaze on Chinese porcelain.

clue.text: Eager son contributed to score increased by 50%

indicators.note: contributed to means put into, so the son's letter goes inside

parts.note: a score is twenty, and half again makes thirty

explanation.surface: A keen son added to the total, raising it by half.
explanation.walkthrough: A score is 20; adding 50% gives THIRTY, with S inside.
explanation.definitionFit: To be thirsty for something is to crave or be keen for it.

clue.text: Expert on telltale features is computing loss after collapse

indicators.note: after a collapse things fall into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A specialist on revealing traits suffers a computer crash and data loss.
explanation.walkthrough: 'features' are newspaper articles, and 'telltale' means gossipy, not revealing.
explanation.definitionFit: A writer of a newspaper column about celebrity scandal is an authority on tittle-tattle articles.

clue.text: Explode loudly after blunder

indicators.note: after places the musical letter behind the word for blunder

parts.note: a goof is a blunder
f stands for forte, loudly, in music

explanation.surface: Someone erupts noisily after making a mistake.
explanation.definitionFit: A bomb or firework is said to go off when it detonates.

clue.text: I am turning up before the game, note

indicators.note: before puts the reversed piece first in the answer
in a down entry, turning up means the letters read from the bottom upward

parts.note: I'm is the contraction of I am
nim is a game of taking matchsticks from piles

explanation.surface: Someone arrives ahead of the match and writes a note.
explanation.walkthrough: I'M reversed gives MI, then NIM.
explanation.definitionFit: A minim is a musical note, a half note lasting two beats.

clue.text: Antelopes love joint of meat I provided

definitions.note: the plural of this antelope's name is the same as its singular

parts.note: love is zero in tennis, written O
a rib is a cut of beef

explanation.surface: Antelopes adore a cut of meat that the speaker supplied.
explanation.definitionFit: The oribi is a small African antelope.

clue.text: Find one Siamese section in Oriental country

indicators.note: section in says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Locating a Thai person somewhere in the East.
explanation.definitionFit: Indonesia is a nation of islands in South-East Asia.

clue.text: Secret society member is to release mother and child

parts.note: to release is to set free
ma is an informal word for mother
a son is a male child

explanation.surface: A member of a secretive order must let a woman and her child go.
explanation.definitionFit: A Mason belongs to a fraternal order famed for its secret rituals.

clue.text: Happen after a month, perhaps

indicators.note: after places the word for happen behind the month in the answer

parts.note: May is a month of the year
to be is to take place or happen

explanation.surface: Something will occur in a month's time, possibly.
explanation.definitionFit: Both words express possibility without certainty.
